exposure: Maternal hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) induced by L-NAME
outcome: Thyroid morphology (follicle size/number, epithelial hyperplasia, endoplasmic reticulum swelling)
Expression of key factors of thyroid hormone synthesis (Ttf1, Pax8, Tshr, Tg, NIS, TSHR)
Endoplasmic reticulum stress indicators (p-IRE1a, ATF6a, XBP1s, Bip)
cohort: Preterm infant rats obtained via Caesarean section delivery from mothers with L-NAME-induced hypertensive disorders of pregnancy or control mothers.
finding: Intrauterine exposure to HDP in preterm infant rats led to significantly higher serum TSH, reduced thyroid follicle size and number, epithelial hyperplasia, endoplasmic reticulum swelling, down-regulation of thyroid hormone synthesis factors, and increased endoplasmic reticulum stress indicators.
